items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So he took me with him and we would play maybe 10 or 15 of these from Friday night over to Sunday... just go from one to the other

ctx.x: Yeah, he was playing -- this was 1927. And he was playing at the Plantation. But I did meet him, actually, at the Warwick Ballroom on 47th Street. On Sunday afternoon they was playing a dance there. But now [unintelligible] I had an opportunity to try out for a band which was called the "Society Syncopaters." And before the rehearsal we had a jam session and everybody was so thrilled with me because, you know, I was playing all the Coleman Hawkins stuff, and alto at that time, you know.

So now the leader was happy, he was going to get me a job with the band. So now the rehearsal started. Well then they found out I couldn't read. So the leader was very nice. He said to me, "well, you play very good but you've got to learn how to read." But, he said, I have a man that maybe can help you out. So he gave me the phone number and address of a man, a piano player named Bill Fry.

Well, I met Bill Fry and Bill Fry was a piano player that played by ear. And he played all the house rent parties -- we called them chittling struts then. And they played all the house rent parties on the weekend around Chicago. So he took me with him and we would play maybe 10 or 15 of these
